events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Day of Rest

options.text: Bid [character] to proceed with the plan.
Work faster without using the days of rest.

events.text: [character] attempts to besiege [city] have been slowed by the actions of the defenders, who send out troops each day to undermine the construction of siege weapons and earthworks. But [character] has noticed that for one day each week there is no attack. When the General’s advisors say it is due to the [religion] population of the city, who do no work for one day in deference to their god, he immediately writes to you with a plan: The troops will concentrate building on only those holy days, to progress the siege uninterrupted.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Calling Out the Gods

options.text: Let us see how long the defenders retain their will to fight when they see their gods desert them.
This is pure folly, refuse to waste a general’s life like this.

events.text: [character] rides before the gates of [city] mocking the defenders and challenging them to a fight. But they will not be drawn. In a drastic move, the General asks to perform an old [religion] ritual to draw out the defending gods of the city and consign them to the underworld. Such a spell has a dreadful cost though, as the ritual requires taking his own life. Is the city worth such a sacrifice?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Engineer Siege

options.text: Study the structures for any weaknesses to exploit.
Train your forces to fight within the city.
Learn what you can about the building process.

events.text: The buildings of [city] stand tall, and [character] stares up at them in admiration. His engineering mind is already constructing and deconstructing them in his mind. [character] asks to lead a reconnaissance mission in the city to study everything he can about the enemy city. Where will you focus his attention?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Jailed Spy

options.text: Install her as an officer in [city].
Bring her to court to advise.

events.text: Recent assaults on [city] have resulted in crowds of prisoners, a few of whom are native [rival]. One of these captives is a former [rival] military student jailed for suspected spying. We should put her to work supporting our current military campaign.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: New Recruits

options.text: Arm them and send them into battle.

events.text: Seizing portions of [city], our soldiers encounter [rival] jails full of foreign captives. Once freed, many of these prisoners offer to replenish our forces on the front lines. Shall these prisoners join our military ranks, or do we grant them asylum in [city]?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Tact and Tactics

options.text: What would I do without you, [character].
I think I have the matter well in hand, thank you very much.

events.text: As advances on the [rival] front bear fruit, [character] has become increasingly enthusiastic about sharing his passion and expertise in siege techniques. "You're doing great in [city]. No, really, dear! But, have you considered, just a tad deeper tunneling behind the north-eastern ramparts?"
